subject.title: Adopt noUncheckedIndexedAccess via a ratchet lane (phase 1: eight small packages)

question: Should phase 1 include exported generic invariant helpers, or should it be limited to the strict compiler/lint/check ratchet and local domain-specific fixes?
rationale: The strictness migration is roadmap-aligned, but exporting generic helpers is a lasting API and design choice that is not required to establish the compiler lane.

options.title: Narrow ratchet phase
options.body: Implement the strict subproject and routing for the eight packages, using local or domain-specific guards and deferring shared exports until repeated need is demonstrated.

options.title: Approve full proposal
options.body: Treat the strict lane, scoped lint rule, package fixes, and generic `normalization-core` exports as one coordinated phase.

options.title: Split architecture first
options.body: Approve and land only the canonical strict-lane infrastructure before separately tracking package migrations and helper APIs.

recommendation.title: Narrow ratchet phase
recommendation.body: Implement the strict subproject and routing for the eight packages, using local or domain-specific guards and deferring shared exports until repeated need is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and most recently maintained the exact compiler and changed-check architecture this decision extends.
